source_documents.title: Probing the potential for anti-Kasha behavior through direct measurements of S2 lifetimes in xanthione and thioxanthone

conditions_studied: solution: series of nonpolar, polar and H-bonding solvents (fs transient absorption, steady-state emission)

reference_evidence_units.quote: This reaffirmation of the broad applicability of the energy gap law suggests that where a molecule exhibits unexpectedly large “anti-Kasha” emission that result must be discussed in terms of particular features of vibronic coupling in that molecule.
reference_evidence_units.subject: XT, TX
reference_evidence_units.statement: S2 lifetimes follow the energy gap law.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Summarizing, the present experimental and computational data on XT show that in line with earlier studies, this molecule indeed exhibits anti-Kasha emission with an S2 lifetime of 10–20 ps.
reference_evidence_units.subject: XT

reference_evidence_units.quote: Between XT and TX, a decrease in Eg by 60% (1.2–0.5 eV – adiabatic energies) leads to an exponential acceleration in S2 → S1 IC from 10–20 to 0.4 ps, accompanied by the expected decrease in “anti-Kasha” S2 emission intensity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: XT vs TX
reference_evidence_units.statement: A smaller S2-S1 gap speeds S2→S1 IC 25-50 fold and weakens S2 emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The dominant relaxation is the 18.5 ps component assigned to the S2 to T1 relaxation on the basis of the associated spectral evolution [Fig. 3(b)].
reference_evidence_units.subject: XT
reference_evidence_units.statement: S2 decays mainly to T1 in 18.5 ps.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Thus, the present calculations are consistent with a long S2 excited state lifetime in XT, with the tens of picoseconds relaxation likely arising through S2 /S1 vibronic coupling, and not via traversing the MECI.
reference_evidence_units.subject: XT
reference_evidence_units.statement: The S2/S1 conical intersection needs a 1 eV uphill out-of-plane distortion and is not the decay route.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We suggest (following the work of Rai-Constapel et al.33 ) that H-bonding solvents lead to a level inversion in the ground state absorption so that the TX bright state becomes the S1 ππ∗ state, which then decays by ISC to a ππ∗ triplet state in competition with fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TX
reference_evidence_units.statement: In protic solvents ππ*/nπ* inversion makes the bright state S1, which competes ISC with fluorescence.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: S2 emission survives because the large S2-S1 gap slows internal conversion (energy gap law); state order and gap explain the anti-Kasha emission (author decision 2026-11-16).

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: S2 relaxes mainly to T1 in 18.5 ps.

contrast_group.varied_factor: sulfur as thiocarbonyl (xanthione) vs ring sulfur with a carbonyl (thioxanthone)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The S2-S1 gap drops from about 1.2 to 0.5 eV, S2→S1 internal conversion speeds up from 10-20 ps to 0.4 ps and S2 emission weakens, as the energy gap law predicts.
